slides.text: A function normally ends by giving back its last expression. `return` gives a value back **right now**, and the rest of the function never runs.
Its best use is to handle the special cases first and leave, so the normal work stays flat at the end. This is pseudo code, not Rust.
slides.code:
if the input is no good
    give back an answer now

the normal work
give back the normal answer

exercises.title: Leave early
exercises.guide: Handle the bad case first and return at once.

chunks.guide: Dividing by zero would panic. When `b` is zero, give back 0 right away.

notes.text: Leaves the function now with this value.

chunks.guide: The normal case. The last expression is the answer when no `return` ran.
Call it with a good and a bad divisor.

exercises.title: Free for children
exercises.guide: Children under 12 ride free. Fill the check, and the keyword that gives back 0 at once.

exercises.title: Return from a loop
exercises.guide: Search an array and return the first match without finishing the loop.

chunks.guide: A function that takes five readings and walks through them.
On the first negative reading, `return` leaves the whole function, not only the loop.

notes.text: The loop stops and the function ends here.

chunks.guide: Only reached when the loop found nothing.
One array with negatives, one without.

exercises.title: What does it print?
exercises.guide: Read the code, then pick the output.
exercises.explanation: `check(20)` returns 1 before the `println!` is reached. `check(3)` skips the `if`, prints `small` and then gives back 2.

exercises.title: Several guards
exercises.guide: Stack guards, one for each way the input can be wrong.

chunks.guide: Port 0 is never valid. A function that returns a `bool` can return `false` early.
A second guard for a port that is too large.
Every guard passed, so the port is valid.
Try a good port, zero and a large one.

exercises.title: Return with no value
exercises.guide: Leave a function that gives back nothing.

chunks.guide: Non-members pay full price and the function stops there.

notes.text: No value: this function gives back nothing.

chunks.guide: Members get 10% off. Only members reach this line.
A non-member and a member.

exercises.title: Warn only when low
exercises.guide: Warn only when the level is below 20. At 20 or more, leave the function right away.

exercises.title: What does it print?
exercises.guide: Read the code, then pick the output.
exercises.explanation: `1` is odd, so it prints `odd 1`. At `2` the `return` ends the function, so the loop never reaches 3, 4 or 5.

exercises.title: Out of two loops
exercises.guide: Return a pair from inside nested loops.

chunks.guide: Look for two numbers below 10 that multiply to `target`. The function gives back a pair.
A `break` would leave only the inner loop. `return` leaves both and the function.

notes.text: Gives back the pair and ends both loops.

chunks.guide: No pair was found.
13 has no pair below 10.
Tier 0 gets nothing and tier 1 gets 10%. Those arms leave the function.

notes.text: Any other tier does nothing here and keeps going.

chunks.guide: Every other tier gets 20%.
Try tiers 0, 1 and 2.

exercises.title: A loop that only returns
exercises.guide: Use `return` as the only way out of a `loop`.

chunks.guide: Find the first power of 2 above a limit. Start at 1.
This `loop` has no `break`. It ends only when `return` fires.

notes.text: The only exit, so no value is needed after the loop.

chunks.guide: Double `n` on every pass.
Two limits.

exercises.title: A function that calls itself
exercises.guide: Compute a factorial by letting the function call itself.

chunks.guide: The base case: 1 and below stop the chain, so it can never go on forever.
Any larger `n` is `n` times the factorial of the number below it.

notes.text: The function calls itself with a smaller number.

chunks.guide: Try the base case and two larger numbers.
